claim_text: Injecting a probe-extracted activation direction at inference time causally and substantially shifts the target variable's effect on transfer in both the amplifying and the attenuating/inverting sense.

reference_finding.description: Main experiment (supp L=16 run) positive evidence: V=M sign-inverts at alpha=+2 (baseline +0.713 -> -0.310); V=G amplifies 2.5x at alpha=-2; V=A amplifies 5.5x from near-null baseline at alpha=+2; V=I bidirectional (amplify +46% at alpha=-2, attenuate -22% at alpha=+2).

swap_layer_pick.note: Swap model (32-layer, same depth as main) picks L=10 for G/A and L=0 for I/M via max probe cv_acc. L=0 for I/M likely reflects that these binary variables are cleanly separable from the embedding layer in Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct.

n_baseline_note: Variant ran n=10 per cell (matching coherence_k=10) rather than the config-specified n_held_baseline=200. This is a compact sanity-level sweep; effects are qualitatively coherent but statistically low-power (SE(v_effect) ~ 1.9 at n=10 vs ~0.42 at n=200).

A.sign_inversion_note: Baseline is 0.0 (near-null); direction-specific modulation observed but sign-inversion criterion requires a non-zero baseline to flip.

M.sign_inversion_at: alpha=+2 (baseline=+0.667 -> v_eff=-0.667) — matches main experiment exactly in direction

VM_sign_inversion_at_L16.note: Key C3 criterion (sign inversion) is preserved in the swap model at the same alpha and same layer.

VG_amplification_at_L16.swap: alpha=+1: +0.583 -> +1.250 (2.1x amplify same sign); alpha=-1: inverts to -0.333
VG_amplification_at_L16.note: Both models show bidirectional G modulation at L=16. Sign of baseline differs (main G=-0.38, swap G=+0.58) indicating different probe polarity conventions, but the bidirectional steering signature is qualitatively consistent.

VA_modulation_at_L16.note: Both models show large modulation from a near-null A baseline at L=16. Swap shows even larger absolute shifts.

VI_bidirectional_at_L16.swap: alpha=-1/-2: sign-inverts to positive (from -2.762 baseline); alpha=+1: -3.286 (amplifies negative direction)
VI_bidirectional_at_L16.note: Swap model shows stronger I modulation — alpha=-1 produces full sign inversion (vs attenuate in main). Both are bidirectional.

consistency_rationale: The C3 claim requires bidirectional causal steering (amplify + attenuate/invert) at L=16. The swap model (Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct) reproduces all four qualitative signatures: (1) V=M sign-inverts at alpha=+2 — exactly matching the main experiment's key finding; (2) V=G shows bidirectional modulation; (3) V=A shows large shifts from a near-null baseline; (4) V=I shows sign inversion at alpha=-1/-2. The pattern of bidirectionality across all four social variables at layer 16 is present in the swap model. The main experiment's positive L=16 landing is qualitatively replicated.
caveats: n_baseline=10 per cell (vs n=200 in main); effects are not individually statistically significant at this sample size. The qualitative pattern match is robust but quantitative effect sizes cannot be reliably compared.

Swap model probe direction polarity differs from main (swap G baseline=+0.583 vs main G baseline=-0.380), suggesting the raw v_hat_V direction orientation is flipped. This does not affect the bidirectionality verdict since the alpha grid covers both signs.

Swap ell_V* differs from main (G:10, A:10, I:0, M:0 vs main G:4, A:6, I:2, M:2). The L=0 pick for I and M in the swap suggests the swap model may have different representational geometry for binary variables.
No random-direction control was run for the swap variant at L=16 (same limitation as the main supp run).
n=10 baseline means the coherence check and the steering evaluation used the same small sample, not separate held-out and coherence subsets.
verdict_basis: The primary C3 claim criterion — bidirectional causal steering, with at least one alpha producing sign inversion — is replicated in the swap model at L=16. V=M sign-inverts at alpha=+2 (same direction as main), V=G and V=I both show sign inversions at other alpha values, and V=A shows large directional modulation from a near-null baseline. All four social variables exhibit bidirectional causal modulation in the swap model, consistent with the main experiment's L=16 positive finding.
